focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I lead a regional nonprofit newsroom.
e002	A large video platform wants to feature a weekly local-investigations program and guarantee the first year of revenue.
e003	That money would cover production and part of a reporter's salary.
e004	The reach could be much larger than our website, and our membership growth has slowed enough that “we own the audience relationship” is starting to sound less comforting when the audience is small.
e005	The platform wants early access, a consistent episode format, and rights to promote clips through recommendations we cannot see or predict.
e006	Editors worry that stories which work on the platform will gradually become the investigations we choose.
e007	Our video editor says that is condescending to the format and that tighter storytelling could improve our work.
e008	I do not want to confuse distribution with capture.
e009	I also do not want a guaranteed year to make dependency look like an abstract future problem.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e010	Separate financing, distribution, format, data, and editorial authority.
e011	Ask what the platform controls, what audience relationship remains yours, what the second year looks like, and which existing reporting the season displaces.
e012	Smaller owned reach also has a cost.
[Turn 2 USER]
e013	One correction: it does not approve topics or scripts.
e014	It can enforce general policies and wants eighteen-to-twenty-two-minute episodes.
e015	We own the full report and publish it one day later.
e016	Our editor thinks the format discipline could help.
e017	Not every constraint is capture.
[Turn 2 ASSISTANT]
e018	Agreed.
e019	Format can be a craft constraint.
e020	The editorial question is what survives once policy, promotion, and revenue interact with it.
e021	Get the policy and appeal process, preserve publication of every full report under your standards, and track stories altered or abandoned for format reasons.
e022	Test newsletter links on real devices.
e023	One-day exclusivity is less consequential than whether viewers can find your owned reporting record and whether the newsroom can contact any part of the audience later.
[Turn 3 USER]
e024	We would receive views, watch time, broad geography, and referral totals, but not subscriber contact information.
e025	The platform says privacy rules prevent sharing more.
e026	It will let us ask viewers to join our newsletter, although external links may not be prominent on every device.
e027	The guaranteed payment covers the program's production cost plus part of one reporter's salary.
e028	After year one, revenue depends on views.
[Turn 3 ASSISTANT]
e029	The guarantee finances a defined experiment; the post-guarantee model creates a different editorial incentive.
e030	Model the second year without optimistic audience conversion and decide what you will not change merely to preserve view-based revenue.
e031	Test the newsletter path on real devices and treat platform followers as rented reach, not members you can reliably contact.
[Turn 4 USER]
e032	Our investigations editor proposed publishing six episodes before deciding anything about continuation.
e033	The platform wants a twelve-episode season and says promotion will be weak if we do not commit to consistency.
e034	It will not specify how much promotion or where episodes will appear because recommendations change.
e035	We can negotiate an exit after six episodes, but the guarantee would fall by more than half.
[Turn 4 ASSISTANT]
e036	The platform is asking you to exchange commitment for an undefined distribution benefit.
e037	A six-episode exit reduces duration but may also make the test inconclusive if promotion depends on twelve.
e038	Ask for minimum deliverables it actually controls—placement, marketing support, technical production assistance—rather than an algorithmic promise it cannot define.
e039	Keep the decision viable on guaranteed revenue and learning even if recommendation exposure is modest.
[Turn 5 USER]
e040	They offered two homepage placements during the season and a named partner manager but will not guarantee recommendation volume.
e041	We can remove our archive if the agreement ends, yet clips already shared by users may persist.
e042	The contract draft also permits the platform to use short excerpts to promote the service for three years.
e043	Our lawyer is reviewing that language, so I do not yet know whether we can limit the contexts or attach our branding.
[Turn 5 ASSISTANT]
e044	Those reuse terms affect reputation and control after the season, so they are not a minor legal appendix.
e045	Do not decide until the permitted contexts, duration, attribution, removal rights, and treatment of sensitive sources are clear.
e046	The two placements are concrete; recommendation volume remains an upside scenario.
e047	Preserve the exact draft and evaluate the revised rights rather than the platform's verbal description.
[Turn 6 USER]
e048	The board chair wants an answer in principle before the next meeting because the platform is scheduling its autumn slate.
e049	I can say we are interested subject to rights and editorial protections, but the editors worry that even a public expression of interest will create momentum.
e050	On the other hand, refusing to signal interest may cause us to lose the slot before the lawyer finishes.
e051	We have not agreed internally what second-year economics would be unacceptable.
[Turn 6 ASSISTANT]
e052	An expression of interest should name the unresolved conditions and avoid announcing the program.
e053	Internally, define the minimum contract rights, acceptable first-year commitment, and second-year decision rule before the timetable turns them into formalities.
e054	Ask the platform for a short written hold while the reuse language is reviewed.
e055	If it refuses, the cost of its urgency becomes part of the offer.
[Turn 7 USER]
e056	My position is to send a private, nonbinding statement of interest conditioned on acceptable excerpt rights, source protection, our ability to publish every full report, and an exit structure the editors can support.
e057	I will not seek board approval for the season until the lawyer returns the draft and we model year two without guaranteed revenue or assumed algorithmic reach.
e058	We still need to decide whether twelve episodes are enough learning to justify the attention the project will take from our existing reporting.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e059	That is a disciplined position: remain in the negotiation without treating uncertain promotion as value already received.
e060	A private statement of interest preserves the autumn possibility while the lawyer resolves reuse and source protection, editors price what twelve episodes displace, and finance models year two without optimism.
e061	Keep external communication quiet until those inputs exist.
e062	You do not yet have a complete offer to approve or reject, but you have reduced the remaining questions to conditions the contract and editorial calendar can answer.
[Turn 8 USER]
e063	The lawyer's draft improved the easy part and exposed the hard part.
e064	Promotional excerpt rights now end one year after the contract and carry our branding, but compilations already produced can stay online.
e065	More importantly, we may withhold a source-risk excerpt only after explaining the concern to the platform's legal team.
e066	Our investigations editor said the explanation itself could reveal what an outside lawyer has no right to know.
e067	So we have “source protection” in the summary and a process that may require us to compromise it in order to invoke it.
e068	That does not feel like one remaining legal detail.
[Turn 8 ASSISTANT]
e069	You are right; I described the remaining issues as contract conditions without distinguishing one that reaches editorial duty.
e070	Source-risk designation must be newsroom-controlled or use a dispute process that does not require sensitive disclosure.
e071	Also define the fate and correction of old compilations.
e072	The exception mechanism, not the friendly summary, determines control.
[Turn 9 USER]
e073	Editors mapped the twelve episodes against our current calendar.
e074	Producing them would delay two investigations unless we hire a freelance producer, which the guarantee can fund.
e075	One delayed investigation concerns municipal contracting and may become time-sensitive.
e076	The platform format could also make that reporting accessible to a much larger local audience.
e077	Opportunity cost is not simply platform work versus serious work; some serious work fits the format and some does not.
[Turn 9 ASSISTANT]
e078	Build the season from editorial priorities first, then test which stories fit without distortion.
e079	Protect time-sensitive investigations regardless of format and price the freelance capacity honestly.
e080	Track stories accelerated, delayed, reformatted, or declined because of the partnership.
e081	The evaluation should ask what reporting the newsroom produced and lost, not whether video is inherently less serious.
[Turn 10 USER]
e082	Our community advisory group was split.
e083	Younger members said our existing site is effectively invisible to many people and warned that independence without reach can become self-congratulation.
e084	Others said the platform's comments and recommendation culture may reward outrage and make local subjects less willing to participate.
e085	They asked whether every episode could have a permanent page on our site with documents, corrections, and ways to contact the newsroom.
[Turn 10 ASSISTANT]
e086	Create a permanent owned page for every episode with documents, corrections, and contact.
e087	Link it wherever the platform permits.
e088	Also plan moderation and subject communication; distribution changes the audience environment even when the reporting does not.
[Turn 11 USER]
e089	The platform extended the deadline by two weeks, which helps, but it wants to list us publicly as a prospective autumn partner before the board votes.
e090	It calls the list nonbinding and says its sales team needs it.
e091	I declined.
e092	The board chair thinks I made the negotiation harder to protect against psychological momentum rather than substance.
e093	That is possible.
e094	Publicly associating our name may also be part of what the platform is buying before it pays us or resolves the source clause.
e095	Once staff, donors, and other outlets see the announcement, a board no will look like a failed deal rather than an ordinary decision.
e096	I want the board to decide first.
e097	I also want to be honest that preserving that governance may cost us the slot.
[Turn 11 ASSISTANT]
e098	Declining the announcement preserves governance and does have a negotiation cost.
e099	Record both rather than calling it obviously prudent.
e100	Ask whether the platform can hold production capacity privately until the vote and what it will withdraw if it cannot publicize the relationship.
e101	The answer will clarify whether early signaling is incidental planning or part of the value it seeks from you.
[Turn 12 USER]
e102	I am still not asking the board to approve the season.
e103	I will return when the source-risk exception is newsroom-controlled, the owned episode pages and correction links are confirmed, and we have a budget that protects the time-sensitive investigation while showing what other work twelve episodes displace.
e104	The second-year model will assume no guaranteed revenue and modest audience conversion.
e105	We remain interested, but an autumn slot and improved excerpt term are not enough to decide whether this is a distribution experiment we control or the start of a dependency we have not priced.
[Turn 12 ASSISTANT]
e106	The current position is a continuation of negotiation, not indecision about a complete offer.
e107	Later work improved reuse rights but exposed a source-protection process the newsroom cannot accept as written.
e108	The editorial calendar made displaced work concrete, the community group clarified that reach and independence are both real values, and the owned episode page gives platform distribution an accountable home.
e109	Preserve every draft, the story calendar before and after freelance capacity, the community disagreement, device tests, the declined announcement, and the conservative second-year model.
e110	The board can decide when source authority, owned records, and protected reporting capacity are concrete.
e111	Before then, a yes would rely on recommendation reach and rights you do not possess; a no would discard a potentially valuable distribution experiment before its actual terms are known.

packet.question: How did the working position or decision change, and does any unresolved qualification remain capable of changing it?
